nodes.summary: Dense CNF-SAT is NP-complete: it lies in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to dense CNF-SAT.
nodes.title: Cook-Levin for dense CNF-SAT

nodes.summary: Every decision problem $L$ in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to dense CNF-SAT: a polynomial-time computable map $f$ on bit strings such that, for every bit string $x$, $L$ accepts $x$ exactly when dense CNF-SAT accepts $f(x)$.
nodes.title: Every NP problem reduces to dense CNF-SAT

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a finite multi-stack Turing machine and let $a$ be a symbol of its output-stack alphabet. In the tableau encoding of $M$ with $a$ adjoined to the output alphabet, some index of the effective output-stack alphabet decodes to $a$.

nodes.title: Tableau encoding with a chosen accept symbol

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a polynomial-time Turing machine that computes a Boolean function on pairs of bit strings, reading a pair $(a, y)$ as the bits of $a$, a separator, then the bits of $y$, and writing its answer as one bit. For every polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients, the reduction built from $V$ and $p$ is polynomial-time computable with respect to the canonical bit-string encodings.
nodes.title: The Cook–Levin reduction is polynomial-time

nodes.summary: For a finite multi-stack Turing machine $M$, a symbol $a$ of its output-stack alphabet and a stack $k$, this is the finite set of symbols that some statement of $M$ can push on stack $k$ (together with the whole input alphabet when $k$ is the input stack), with $a$ added when $k$ is the output stack.

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a polynomial-time machine computing a function of pairs of bit lists from their pair encoding, with time polynomial $t_V$. This is a natural number $c \ge 1$, fixed by choice, such that for some exponent $e$ we have $t_V(j) \le (j + c)^e$ for every natural number $j$.

This is an exponent $e$, fixed by choice, with $t_V(j) \le (j + c)^e$ for every natural number $j$.

This is the symbol of $V$'s input alphabet that corresponds to the separator $\#$, the element $\mathrm{inr}(\mathrm{none})$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
